title: Ecuador open data for your AI assistant

More answers from your data. Ecuador publishes a huge amount of public data, but finding it means navigating different portals, checking separate catalogs, and guessing which file is current. EcuDataMCP gives your AI assistant the tools to do that work for you, and still cites the official source in every answer. How it works A traceable path. Four steps, from natural language to the official source. 01 Search search_ecuador searches datasets, procedures, regulations, contracts, and risk events by keyword, all at once. 02 Inspect get_dataset_info and list_dataset_resources check fields, formats, and dates before pulling any data. 03 Query query_resource_data filters the CKAN DataStore without downloading the whole file, or preview_resource_data for CSV, JSON, and XLSX. 04 Cite Every result links back to the official source (the dataset, the procedure, the SERCOP record) so you can verify it. Notice: Some tool definitions, parameters and descriptions were generated or assisted by AI. They may be incomplete or outdated; a tool may return partial results, reject valid parameters, or behave unexpectedly when the official source changes. Always check the response against the linked source and manually review results before using them for important decisions. What can you ask? Ask in plain language, without searching portal by portal. 60 official sources, in a single conversation. “What data does the SRI have on tax collection?” “Show me INEC's health datasets” “What are the requirements for getting a passport?” “Which retail-sector companies had the highest ROE this year?” “Look up this public tender in SERCOP” “How has consumer confidence changed according to the BCE over the last two years?” “Find a BCE IEM table on exports and show me its latest values.” “Which public SRI cubes are available for aggregate queries?” Sources Official data, always cited. EcuDataMCP never copies or stores these catalogs: every query goes live against the source portal. 60 sources grouped by theme — Central Bank, SRI, INEC, Supercías, Superbancos and more — each tied to its own institution. Open data catalogs Procedures, regulations & public procurement Risk & natural hazards Economy & finance Statistics & demographics Agriculture Energy Labour & employment Oversight & transparency Transport & civil aviation Health Telecommunications International sources with an Ecuador angle See the 60 sources, grouped → The backstage Open-source MCP server. EcuDataMCP runs as a Python server built with the official MCP SDK , exposed over Streamable HTTP or stdio. There is no database of its own: every tool calls the matching official portal live (CKAN, gob.ec, SERCOP, BCE, Supercías, IG-EPN, SGR) and returns the formatted response. ‹ gob.ec INEC BCE SRI Supercías Superbancos Contraloría IESS SEPS CENACE SGR INEVAL DGAC ARCSA › See the 82 tools in the Reference → Connect your assistant Copy your client's configuration. Run the server locally (Docker or uv run , see the README ) and point your MCP client at http://localhost:8000/mcp . The Docker compose file requires a token: set MCP_AUTH_TOKEN (or MCP_REQUIRE_AUTH=0 for local use only). For a local stdio client, the simplest option is uvx ecuador-mcp --transport stdio . Quick start Copy uv sync && uv run python main.py --transport http --port 8000 Quick option If your assistant has terminal access, hand it the repo link and let it install everything for you: Copy Clone https://github.com/DweskZ/EcuDataMCP, install its dependencies with uv sync, and register it as an MCP server in my client using stdio mode with `uv run --directory <clone-path> python main.py --transport stdio`. Verify the server responds before calling it done. Always review what your assistant changes (config files, commands run) before confirming. This option only works with assistants that can run commands on their own: today that's Claude Code , Codex , Cursor , and Windsurf in agent mode. With ChatGPT, chat-only Claude.ai, or other terminal-less clients, use the manual configuration below. Claude Desktop Cursor VS Code ChatGPT Claude Code Codex Gemini CLI Le Chat (Mistral) Windsurf HuggingChat Add this to your Claude Desktop config file ( ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json on macOS, %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json on Windows): Copy { "mcpServers": { "ecuador-datos": { "command": "npx", "args": [ "mcp-remote", "http://localhost:8000/mcp" ] } } } Open Cursor Settings Search for "MCP" Add a new MCP server: Copy { "mcpServers": { "ecuador-datos": { "url": "http://localhost:8000/mcp", "transport": "http" } } } Add to your mcp.json file (run MCP: Open User Configuration from the command palette): Copy { "servers": { "ecuador-datos": { "url": "http://localhost:8000/mcp", "type": "http" } } } *Available on paid plans (Plus, Pro, Team, Enterprise).* Go to Settings > Apps and connectors Open Advanced settings and enable Developer mode In Settings > Connectors > Browse connectors , click Add a new connector Set the URL: http://localhost:8000/mcp Copy claude mcp add --transport http ecuador-datos http://localhost:8000/mcp Saves the configuration to ~/.codex/config.toml (an [mcp_servers.ecuador-datos] block with url ). To use the server over stdio instead of HTTP: codex mcp add ecuador-datos -- uvx ecuador-mcp --transport stdio . Copy codex mcp add ecuador-datos --url http://localhost:8000/mcp Add to ~/.gemini/settings.json : Copy { "mcpServers": { "ecuador-datos": { "httpUrl": "http://localhost:8000/mcp" } } } Go to Intelligence > Connectors Add connector > Custom MCP Connector Name: "Ecuador Datos" / URL: http://localhost:8000/mcp Add to ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json : Copy { "mcpServers": { "ecuador-datos": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "http://localhost:8000/mcp"] } } } In the chat, click the + icon > MCP Servers > Manage MCP Servers Add Server with name "Ecuador Datos" and URL http://localhost:8000/mcp Troubleshooting Something not working? Start by confirming the server is alive. If it responds, the problem is almost always in the client configuration or the upstream portal, not in EcuDataMCP. Copy curl http://localhost:8000/health It should return {"status":"ok", "version": ...} . If it doesn't respond, the server isn't running or is listening on a different port. My client shows no tools Check, in order: (1) the server is running ( /health responds); (2) the URL ends in /mcp , not / or /health ; (3) the config JSON is valid (one stray comma silently breaks it); and (4) you fully restarted the client after editing the config. Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Windsurf only read the file at startup. Claude Desktop or Windsurf: npx not found Those configs use mcp-remote as a bridge, which needs Node.js 18+ installed and on the PATH . Install it from nodejs.org and restart the client. Node-free alternative: use stdio mode with "command": "uv" and "args": ["run", "--directory", "<clone-path>", "python", "main.py", "--transport", "stdio"] . Port 8000 is already in use Start the server on another port ( uv run main.py --port 8007 , or MCP_PORT=8007 docker compose up -d ) and change the client URL to http://localhost:8007/mcp . In stdio mode the server exits immediately Run the same command by hand in a terminal to see the real error. Typical causes are a wrong --directory path, not having run uv sync in the clone, or uv not being on the PATH the client sees (in that case, use the absolute path to uv ). ChatGPT or Le Chat can't reach localhost Web clients run in the cloud and can't see your machine. You need to expose the server at a public HTTPS URL (a tunnel or your own deployment) and, in that case, enable MCP_REQUIRE_AUTH=1 with an MCP_AUTH_TOKEN . Never expose the server without a token. 401, 429, or 503 error from the server 401 : the server requires a token ( MCP_AUTH_TOKEN ) and the client isn't sending it as Authorization: Bearer ... . 429 : you exceeded the per-window request limit ( MCP_RATE_LIMIT_REQUESTS , 120 per 60 s by default); wait, or raise it for local use. 503 : too many concurrent requests ( MCP_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS , 8 by default). 403 error or timeout from the Open Data portal www.datosabiertos.gob.ec sometimes rejects connections coming from outside Latin America (403 error). If you see this, run the server from a connection with an exit point in Ecuador or the region (a VPN, for example). The procedures and institutions tools use a different portal and don't have this issue. Government portals also have their own outages: if a single tool fails while the rest respond, try again later. TLS / SSL certificate error Some official portals have served expired certificates or incomplete chains (the Open Data portal's expired in July 2026). For that portal there's an opt-in retry: CKAN_INSECURE_TLS=1 in your .env . Use it only while the portal is broken and remove it afterward. The preview is cut off or says the file is too large That's intentional: downloads are capped at 5 MB and ZIP/tar.gz decompression at 20 MB. For large resources use query_resource_data (filters in the CKAN DataStore without downloading the file) or list_zip_contents to see what a ZIP contains before opening it. I need more detail to report a bug Start with LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG , reproduce the error, and open a GitHub issue with the tool, its parameters, the /health output, and the log. Don't include tokens. No friction Ready to use, no setup of your own. No API key All sources are public data, no authentication. (The HTTP endpoint can be protected with your own token, MCP_AUTH_TOKEN .) No account There is no sign-up or user account to create. 100% public data Under an open license, exactly as the Ecuadorian state publishes it. No telemetry The server runs on your machine and sends your queries to no one; it only keeps local per-tool usage counters (never the arguments). FAQ Got more questions? What is EcuDataMCP? An open-source MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that helps your AI assistant discover and query Ecuador's open government data: datasets, procedures, regulations, public contracts, risk events, earthquakes, Central Bank indicators, and companies. What is MCP? Model Context Protocol is an open standard for connecting AI assistants to external tools and data sources, while keeping control over what the model can do and what data it can read. What assistants can I use? Any MCP-compatible client: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT (paid plans), Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI, Le Chat, Windsurf, HuggingChat, and more. Do I need an API key? No. Every source the server uses is public data with no authentication. Is this an official service of the Ecuadorian government? No. EcuDataMCP is an independent, open-source project that queries the same public sources the Ecuadorian state already publishes. It is not affiliated with any institution. Does the server store my questions? There is no external telemetry. The server runs locally on your machine, and every query goes straight from the MCP client to the matching official portal. The only thing recorded is local per-tool usage counters (name, outcome and duration, never the arguments). What formats does it support? In-memory preview of CSV, TSV, JSON, GeoJSON, and XLSX; filtered tabular queries via the CKAN DataStore when the resource supports it. Something isn't working, where do I look? See the Troubleshooting section: it covers clients that show no tools, busy ports, 401/403/429 errors, TLS certificates, and oversized files. Can I contribute? Yes, the project is MIT-licensed and accepts pull requests. See the guide at Contribute . Ecuador's open data, with your favorite AI assistant. View on GitHub

text: Reference All 82 tools , one by one. Find a tool by name, source, or task. Open only the group and detail you need. 82 tools · open a group to see its details. Expand groups Collapse groups Unified entry points 2 Show search_ecuador Searches datasets, orgs, procedures, regulations, contracts, and risk events all at once. Unified search across Ecuador open data, trámites, regulations, contracts and risk events. Use this as the first step for broad questions. Then drill down with get_dataset_info, query_resource_data, get_tramite_info, get_regulacion_info, get_contrato_info or search_eventos_riesgo. Parameter Type Default Description query str required Search terms in Spanish (e.g. "salud", "RUC", "medicinas") limit int 5 Max results per section (default 5, max 10) format Literal['text', 'json'] text Output format: `text` (default) or `json`. lookup_ubicacion Provinces, cantons, and parishes (INEC code, region, population). Look up Ecuador DPA geography: provinces, cantons and parroquias (INEC codes). - nivel='provincia' | 'canton' | 'parroquia' | 'auto' - For parroquias, filter with canton= and/or provincia= (recommended) Parameter Type Default Description query str empty Name or code (e.g. "Pichincha", "Cuenca", "Tumbaco", "170150") region str empty Optional natural region for provinces/cantons provincia str empty Optional province filter canton str empty Optional canton filter (useful for parroquias) nivel Literal['auto', 'provincia', 'canton', 'parroquia'] auto auto | provincia | canton | parroquia format Literal['text', 'json'] text Output format: `text` (default) or `json`. Open Data 8 Show search_datasets Search datasets by keyword. Supports filtering by category. Search for datasets on Ecuador's open data portal (www.datosabiertos.gob.ec). This is the starting point for exploring government data from 98+ public institutions. Use short, specific queries in Spanish for best results. Typical workflow: search_datasets → list_dataset_resources → preview_resource_data Parameter Type Default Description query str empty Search keywords (e.g. "empleo", "salud", "presupuesto", "SRI recaudación") page int 1 Page number (1-based, default: 1) page_size int 20 Results per page (default: 20, max: 100) category str empty Optional category filter (e.g. "sal" for Salud, "edu" for Educación). Use list_categories to see all available categories. sort Literal['relevance', 'recent'] relevance `relevance` (default, CKAN's own ranking) or `recent` (newest first by metadata_modified; works without a query to discover new or freshly refreshed datasets). source ckan_client.CkanSource nacional "nacional" (default, www.datosabiertos.gob.ec), "cuenca" (cuencaendatos.cuenca.gob.ec, independent municipal portal), "latacunga" (datosabiertos.latacunga.gob.ec, independent municipal portal), or "iadb" (data.iadb.org, IADB's open-data portal — NOT Ecuador-only, a regional/global catalog: Latin Macro Watch and World Bank/IADB indicators) format Literal['text', 'json'] text Output format: `text` (default) or `json`. get_dataset_info Detailed dataset metadata: title, description, organization, tags, license, dates. Get detailed metadata about a specific dataset from Ecuador's open data portal. Returns title, description, organization, tags, resource count, creation/update dates, license, update frequency, the publisher's source URL (where the entity keeps the authoritative data, if any), and any custom metadata fields the publisher added. Parameter Type Default Description dataset_id str required The dataset ID or slug (e.g. "registro-estadistico-de-recursos-y-actividades-de-salud-2019") source ckan_client.CkanSource nacional "nacional" (default, www.datosabiertos.gob.ec), "cuenca" (cuencaendatos.cuenca.gob.ec, independent municipal portal), "latacunga" (datosabiertos.latacunga.gob.ec, independent municipal portal), or "iadb" (data.iadb.org, IADB's open-data portal — NOT Ecuador-only, a regional/global catalog: Latin Macro Watch and World Bank/IADB indicators) format Literal['text', 'json'] text Output format: `text` (default) or `json`. list_dataset_resources Lists all files (resources) in a dataset with format, size, URL, and creation/modification dates. List all resources (files) in a dataset with their metadata. Returns resource ID, title, format, size, download URL, and creation/ last-modified dates for each file. The dates let you tell whether a dataset's files are periodic snapshots (compare last_modified across resources to find the most recent one) before reading any of them. Also flags groups of resources whose names look like a periodic series (e.g. weekly files) — that's only a hint that they might need combining or picking the latest one; it does not tell you which, since that depends on the dataset (some periodic files replace previous ones, others complement them). Next step: use preview_resource_data on a CSV resource to see its contents, or use get_resource_info for detailed metadata. Parameter Type Default Description dataset_id str required The dataset ID or slug source ckan_client.CkanSource nacional "nacional" (default, www.datosabiertos.gob.ec), "cuenca" (cuencaendatos.cuenca.gob.ec, independent municipal portal), "latacunga" (datosabiertos.latacunga.gob.ec, independent municipal portal), or "iadb" (data.iadb.org, IADB's open-data portal — NOT Ecuador-only, a regional/global catalog: Latin Macro Watch and World Bank/IADB indicators) format Literal['text', 'json'] text Output format: `text` (default) or `json`. get_resource_info Detailed information about a specific file. Get detailed information about a specific resource (file) from Ecuador's open data portal. Returns format, size, MIME type, download URL, and dataset association. For CSV files, you can then use preview_resource_data to see the actual data. Parameter Type Default Description resource_id str required The resource UUID source ckan_client.CkanSource nacional "nacional" (default, www.datosabiertos.gob.ec), "cuenca" (cuencaendatos.cuenca.gob.ec, independent municipal portal), "latacunga" (datosabiertos.latacunga.gob.ec, independent municipal portal), or "iadb" (data.iadb.org, IADB's open-data portal — NOT Ecuador-only, a regional/global catalog: Latin Macro Watch and World Bank/IADB indicators) format Literal['text', 'json'] text Output format: `text` (default) or `json`. preview_resource_data Preview CSV/TSV, JSON/GeoJSON, Excel (XLS/XLSX/XLSB), ODS or a ZIP/tar.gz wrapping a CSV as a table (max 5 MB). Download and preview a resource from Ecuador's open data portal. Supports CSV/TSV, JSON/GeoJSON, Excel (XLS/XLSX/XLSB), ODS, and .zip or .tar.gz wrapping a CSV/TSV/TXT. Returns the first N rows as a formatted table so the model can inspect data without a local download. Geometry/WKT columns are dropped from the table (they can be tens of KB per cell); CSV columns in European decimal notation (7.760,2) are normalized to standard notation (7760.2). Max download size: 5 MB. For large tabular DataStore resources prefer query_resource_data. Parameter Type Default Description resource_id str required The resource UUID (get it from list_dataset_resources) rows int 20 Number of data rows to preview (default: 20, max: 100) source ckan_client.CkanSource nacional "nacional" (default, www.datosabiertos.gob.ec), "cuenca" (cuencaendatos.cuenca.gob.ec, independent municipal portal), "latacunga" (datosabiertos.latacunga.gob.ec, independent municipal portal), or "iadb" (data.iadb.org, IADB's open-data portal — NOT Ecuador-only, a regional/global catalog: Latin Macro Watch and World Bank/IADB indicators) format Literal['text', 'json'] text Output format: `text` (default) or `json`. download_resource Raw base64 bytes of a resource (max 5 MB) for formats preview_resource_data can't parse (.rar or unrecognized). Download a resource's raw bytes from Ecuador's open data portal, base64-encoded. Use this for formats preview_resource_data can't parse into a table (.rar or anything unrecognized) — it fetches the file as-is instead of trying to read it. Max size: 5 MB (same cap as preview_resource_data). Larger files come back with an error and the direct URL instead, since they'd be too big to embed in a response. Call with format="json" to get the actual file content — the default format="text" only confirms the download and never includes content_base64. Parameter Type Default Description resource_id str required The resource UUID (get it from list_dataset_resources) source ckan_client.CkanSource nacional "nacional" (default, www.datosabiertos.gob.ec), "cuenca" (cuencaendatos.cuenca.gob.ec, independent municipal portal), "latacunga" (datosabiertos.latacunga.gob.ec, independent municipal portal), or "iadb" (data.iadb.org, IADB's open-data portal — NOT Ecuador-only, a regional/global catalog: Latin Macro Watch and World Bank/IADB indicators) format Literal['text', 'json'] text Output format: `text` (default) or `json`. query_resource_data Tabular query via the CKAN DataStore (filters, text, pagination) without downloading the file. Query a tabular resource via CKAN DataStore without downloading the full file. Prefer this over preview_resource_data when the resource is in the DataStore (most CSV resources on the portal). Supports full-text query, JSON filters, sorting and pagination. Parameter Type Default Description resource_id str required Resource UUID (from list_dataset_resources) query str empty Optional full-text search across datastore fields filters_json str empty Optional JSON object of exact field filters, e.g. '{"provincia":"Pichincha"}' rows int 20 Number of records to return (default 20, max 100) offset int 0 Pagination offset (default 0) sort str empty Optional sort expression, e.g. "anio desc" source ckan_client.CkanSource nacional "nacional" (default, www.datosabiertos.gob.ec), "cuenca" (cuencaendatos.cuenca.gob.ec, independent municipal portal), "latacunga" (datosabiertos.latacunga.gob.ec, independent municipal portal), or "iadb" (data.iadb.org, IADB's open-data portal — NOT Ecuador-only, a regional/global catalog: Latin Macro Watch and World Bank/IADB indicators) format Literal['text', 'json'] text Output format: `text` (default) or `json`. detect_series_pattern For datasets that publish one file per period: tells whether each new file replaces the previous ones (cumulative) or complements them (incremental). When a dataset publishes one file per period (weekly/monthly), it's not always clear whether each new file replaces the previous ones (cumulative -- only the newest file matters) or complements them (incremental -- every file must be combined). Downloads the two most recent resources from the periodic-name group list_dataset_resources already detects, finds a date/period-like column by header name (fecha, mes, año, periodo, semana, ...), and compares which period values appear in both files. High overlap → cumulative; near-zero overlap → incremental; if no period column is found or the overlap is ambiguous, returns indeterminado rather than guessing. A heuristic over a sample of up to 500 rows per file -- confirm with preview_resource_data if the result is close to the threshold. Parameter Type Default Description dataset_id str required The dataset ID or slug resource_id_new str | None none Optional -- newer resource ID to compare (auto-detected from the dataset's periodic-name group if omitted) resource_id_old str | None none Optional -- older resource ID to compare (auto-detected if omitted). Both resource_id_new/resource_id_old must be given together, or neither. source ckan_client.CkanSource nacional "nacional" (default, www.datosabiertos.gob.ec), "cuenca" (cuencaendatos.cuenca.gob.ec, independent municipal portal), "latacunga" (datosabiertos.latacunga.gob.ec, independent municipal portal), or "iadb" (data.iadb.org, IADB's open-data portal — NOT Ecuador-only, a regional/global catalog: Latin Macro Watch and World Bank/IADB indicators) format Literal['text', 'json'] text Output format: `text` (default) or `json`. Government procedures 5 Show search_tramites Search Ecuadorian government procedures (ID card, passport, RUC, driver's license, etc.). Search for government procedures (trámites) on Ecuador's official portal gob.ec. Best approach: provide an institution_id to get that institution's trámites. Add a query to filter results by keyword (filters by name and description). When query is provided with institution_id, ALL pages of that institution's trámites are fetched and filtered, so you always get the most relevant results. Common institution IDs: - "8" = SRI (Servicio de Rentas Internas) — impuestos, RUC, facturación - "23" = Registro Civil — cédula, partidas de nacimiento - "62" = ANT — licencias de conducir, matriculación vehicular - "16" = Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores — pasaportes, apostilla - "5" = IESS — seguro social, pensiones, fondos de reserva Use list_instituciones to find more institution IDs. Parameter Type Default Description query str empty Keywords to filter results (e.g. "RUC", "inscripción RUC persona natural"). Each word must appear in the trámite name or description. institution_id str empty Institution ID (strongly recommended for relevant results) page int 1 Page number (1-based, default: 1). Ignored when query is provided (all pages are searched automatically). format Literal['text', 'json'] text Output format: `text` (default) or `json`. get_tramite_info Requirements, beneficiaries, cost and responsible institution of one trámite. Get detailed information about a specific government procedure (trámite). Returns the procedure name, description, requirements, beneficiaries, cost, and the institution responsible. Get the tramite_id from search_tramites. Parameter Type Default Description tramite_id str required The procedure ID (e.g. "18009") format Literal['text', 'json'] text Output format: `text` (default) or `json`. get_tramite_estadisticas Monthly usage/complaint transparency series for one trámite, since 2021. Monthly usage and complaint series (atenciones/quejas) for one specific trámite. Different from get_tramite_info: this is how many people were actually attended each month, and how many complaints were filed, since gob.ec started publishing this (mid-2021). Get tramite_id from search_tramites. There is no bulk endpoint -- this fetches one trámite's series at a time (currently a few dozen months, no pagination needed). Parameter Type Default Description tramite_id str required The procedure ID (e.g. "11752") format Literal['text', 'json'] text Output format: `text` (default) or `json`. list_instituciones List Ecuador's public institutions. List or search public institutions registered on Ecuador's gob.ec portal. If a query is provided, searches across all institutions by name or acronym. Without a query, returns a paginated list. Common institutions: SRI (ID: 8), Registro Civil (ID: 23), ANT (ID: 62), Cancillería (ID: 16), IESS (ID: 5), Ministerio de Salud, INEC, BCE. Parameter Type Default Description query str empty Optional search term (e.g. "SRI", "salud", "rentas") page int 1 Page number (1-based, default: 1, only used without query) format Literal['text', 'json'] text Output format: `text` (default) or `json`. get_institucion_info Detail of an institution (sector, website, description). Get detailed information about a public institution registered on gob.ec. Returns name, acronym, sector, description, website and portal URL. Get the institucion_id from list_instituciones. title: Examples
text: The problem, first Real questions, cited data. Ask a general AI assistant about Ecuador and it's common for it to invent figures with total confidence: there isn't enough Ecuador in the data it was trained on, and it has no way to verify anything in real time. Give it EcuDataMCP's tools and it stops guessing: it searches the official portal, cites the source, and the number it returns is real. These ten examples show that difference. search_sismos “What earthquakes has the Geophysical Institute recorded in Ecuador recently?” Returns the IG-EPN's latest catalog: magnitude, depth, location, and review status (confirmed or reviewed) for each event, with a direct link to the official bulletin. See Sismicidad Ecuador live ↗ www.igepn.edu.ec ↗ And the rest of the universe “How many active taxpayers does the SRI's RUC registry have right now?” search_archivos The most recent registry records 2,904,355 active taxpayers, summing the TOTAL column, not counting rows. sri.gob.ec/datasets ↗ “How many people collected IESS unemployment insurance in June 2026?” query_resource_data June 2026: 2,561 beneficiaries , USD 836,716.99 in total, excluding the TOTAL: row embedded in the file. datosabiertos.gob.ec (IESS) ↗ “What's the WTI oil price right now, per the Central Bank?” get_bce_indicador_diario USD 99.12 per barrel as of September 27, 2026 — the Central Bank's daily series (history back to 2015). contenido.bce.fin.ec ↗ “What are the requirements for getting a passport?” get_tramite_info Proof of payment, a valid ID card, and — if it's a renewal — the previous passport or the loss report, straight from the gob.ec portal. gob.ec ↗ “Who won the school-desks tender for Universidad Técnica Luis Vargas Torres, and for how much?” search_contratos Tito Marcelo Coral Guevara, for USD 130,100 via electronic reverse auction (March 2023). compraspublicas.gob.ec ↗ “How has consumer confidence evolved this year?” get_indicador_bce The Global Consumer Confidence Indicator rose to 36.40 in May 2026, up from 36.07 in March — the BCE's monthly series. contenido.bce.fin.ec ↗ “Which companies have the best ROE in a given sector?” search_ranking A ranking across ~38 financial ratios (liquidity, leverage, profitability), filterable by CIIU code and year. supercias.gob.ec ↗ “Which INEC surveys have downloadable microdata on employment?” search_anda The NADA/IHSN catalog shows exactly which surveys carry downloadable microdata, with the direct link. anda.inec.gob.ec ↗ “What rules regulate a given activity, with an Official Register reference?” get_regulacion_info The regulation's detail, with a direct link to the Official Register PDF. gob.ec ↗ Got a question these sources could answer? title: Releases
text: Releases Fast iteration, real changes. The first releases laid the server's foundation over the initial weeks of development. Since then, each new version corresponds to an added source or a concrete improvement, not a fixed schedule. The full technical detail for every change lives in the CHANGELOG . v0.11.0 2026-10-02 Breaking change in tool names: 90 down to 82 in the default profile. New get_serie_internacional(fuente) with World Bank WDI indicators, IRENA electricity capacity and generation, and XM's Colombia-Ecuador power flows since 2003. list_catalogo(fuente) replaces five listings (ARCONEL, BCE daily indicators, Contraloría, IESS and SUT); get_aviso_aeronautico(tipo) replaces get_metar, get_notam and get_sigmet; search_archivos absorbs BCE remittance, foreign-trade price and publication files and gains a formato filter. XM shows days without flow as 0 GWh, so the October 2024 suspension appears as zeros. v0.10.0 2026-09-28 Breaking change in tool names: 109 down to 90 in the default profile. Every parameter now has a description in the schema. Several tools merge behind a selector: search_archivos(fuente) replaces 11 file searchers (SRI, MEF, Census, MINEDEC, SENESCYT, ARCOTEL and others); search_cortes and get_cortes_horarios cover EEQ and Centrosur; search_capas_geo and get_capa_geo_datos cover the INAMHI and MAG geoportals; search_bce_paginas and get_bce_pagina_archivos cover BCE indices and national accounts. title: About
text: About A bridge between public data and your AI assistant. EcuDataMCP exists because finding a public data point in Ecuador almost always means guessing which portal it's on, under what name, and in what format. The server gives your assistant the tools to do that search for you, and always lets you verify against the official source. History Where it comes from. EcuDataMCP was started in April 2026 by Luis Figueroa ( DweskZ ). Since then, he and Daniel Sánchez Pazmiño have maintained it together: new sources (SRI Datasets, BCE, Supercías auditors), more robust error and download handling, and this site, so connecting the server doesn't depend on reading a README end to end. Independence Not a service of the Ecuadorian state. EcuDataMCP is an independent, open-source project. It queries the same public sources that Ecuadorian government institutions already publish (CKAN, gob.ec, SERCOP, BCE, Supercías, IG-EPN, SGR), but it is not affiliated with, funded by, or endorsed by any of them. Every answer links to the official source precisely so that distinction stays clear: what you see is what the portal publishes, not a copy. License & maintenance MIT, and open for you to use. The full codebase (MCP server and this site) is MIT . It's maintained by Luis Figueroa and Daniel Sánchez Pazmiño . Want to add a source, a tool, or fix something? Start at Contribute . Ecuador's open data, with your favorite AI assistant. View on GitHub

title: Contribute
text: Contribute Add your source , your tool , your idea. EcuDataMCP is MIT-licensed and accepts pull requests. You don't need to be an expert in MCP or the whole project stack: most contributions touch a single piece. Contribution flow Fork, branch, PR. 01 Fork Fork DweskZ/EcuDataMCP to your account. 02 Branch git checkout -b feature/new-tool 03 Commit git commit -m 'feat: add new tool' 04 Pull Request Push to your fork and open a PR describing the change. MCP server Python, uv, pytest. The server lives in tools/ , helpers/ , resources/ , and prompts/ . It requires Python 3.11+ and uv . Copy uv sync uv run pytest uv run ruff check . A new tool is usually three files: the function in tools/ , its registration in tools/__init__.py , and a test in tests/ . Every missing source, every tool short on coverage, is a possible contribution. View on GitHub
